newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone treason suspects plead not guilty.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone treason suspects plead not guilty.

text.p: Nine treason suspects, including soldiers, pleaded not guilty on Thursday to charges of trying to topple the elected civilian government of Sierra Leone in September, court sources said.
The nine, including a woman who heard of the coup but did not pass on details to authorities, have all been charged with treason and face execution if found guilty.
The court, holding its second hearing in the case, adjourned the trial until January.
Confusion reigned about whether or not there had been a second plot to topple President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah and his government.
Newspapers and police sources said six soldiers, three civilians and two Russian helicopter pilots had been arrested in connection with the latest allegations.

The government, keen to project an image of growing stability after signing a peace deal with rebels, neither confirmed nor denied the reports. The sources gave no details of the timing of the second plot.
Tejan Kabbah took office in March after multi-party elections called to end four years of army rule. His government and rebels signed a peace deal in Ivory Coast on November 30.
